title: सुदूरपश्चिममा ट्रान्सजेंडरको अनुभव र अवस्था
nepali: याे लेखले सुदुरपश्चिम प्रदेशमा ट्रान्सजेन्डर (पारलैङ्गिक) व्यक्ति हरू समाजमा आफ्नाे पहिचानका साथ अगाडी आउन सकेका छन्त भन्ने प्रश्ननको उत्तर खाेज्नका लागि, उनीहरुको जीवन भोगाई र अवस्था पत्ता लगाउने उद्देश्य राखेको छ । त्यसको लागि १० जना ट्रान्सजेन्डर व्यक्तीहरुसँग अनलाइन (जूम) र फाेनको माध्ममबाट असंरचित प्रश्नावलीकाे प्रयाेग गरी गहन अन्तर्वार्ता गरिएको थियो। ट्रान्सजेंडरको अनुभव र अवस्था बुझ्दा व्यक्ति विशेष फरक-फरक अवस्था र अनुभव पाइयो l याे अध्ययनको निम्न निष्कर्षहरु रहेका छन् कानुनले ट्रान्सजेंडरलाई समानताको हक प्रदान गरेता पनि प्रयोगमासहज, व्यवहार र सम्बन्धमा परिवर्तन पाइएन l समलिङ्गी विवाहलाई कानुनले मान्यता नदिए तापनि व्यवहारमा विवाह भएको पाइन्छ l अझैपनि प्रायजसो ट्रान्सजेंडरहरु आफुले चाहेको पहिचानका साथ समाजमा आउन नसकेको र केही मात्र भएपनि निलहिरा समाज द्वारा आफ्नो पहिचान निर्माण गरेको पाइन्छ l ट्रान्सजेंडरहरु विभिन्न क्षेत्रबाट विपरीत लिङ्गीकाे व्यवहार भएकै कारण बहिष्कृत हुनुपरेकोले उनीहरूको सामाजिक शैक्षिक र आर्थिक उन्नतिमा बाधा पुगेको देखियो l जसको कारण ट्रान्सजेंडरहरुसँग सम्बन्धित पर्याप्त ज्ञानका साथै ट्रान्सजेंडर अनुकूल वातावरण नहुनु र ट्रान्सजेंडरलाई समाजको एक भागको रूपमा लिई व्यवहार र सम्बन्ध कायम गर्न नसक्नुरहेको छ l ट्रान्सजेंडर मैत्री वातावरण बनाउनका लागि समाज र शैक्षिक प्रणालीमा ट्रान्सजेंडर सम्बन्धी पर्याप्त ज्ञान प्रदान गर्नुका साथै मिडिया प्रयोग गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ l उनीहरूलाई फरक नभएर समान व्यवहार गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ l साथै ट्रान्सजेंडरहरुलाई सशक्तीकरण गरी आत्मसम्मानको जीवन जिउने वातावरण बनाउन सकेमा ट्रान्सजेंडरहरुको जीवन गुणस्तरीय बनाउन सकिन्छ जुन कुरा देशको समृद्धिसँग जोडिन जान्छ l यस अध्ययनले नीति निर्माण र सुधार गर्नमा सहयोग पुर्याउँछ l
american_english: This article seeks to answer the question of whether transgender individuals in Far-Western Province have been able to come forward in society with their identity, and aims to ascertain their life experiences and conditions. To that end, in-depth interviews were conducted with 10 transgender persons using an unstructured questionnaire via online (Zoom) and phone mediums. In understanding the experiences and conditions of transgender people, different individual conditions and experiences were found. The following are the conclusions of this study: Although the law has provided transgender people the right to equality, no change was found in practice, behavior and relationships. Even though the law has not recognized same-sex marriage, marriage was found to exist in practice. Still, most transgender persons have been unable to come out into society with their desired identity, and only a few have been found to have constructed their identity with society's acceptance. Transgender persons have had to face exclusion due to discriminatory behavior from various sectors, and this has been seen to create obstacles in their social, educational and economic advancement. Because of this, it has not been possible to maintain behavior and relationships by regarding transgender people as a part of society, nor has there been a transgender-friendly environment with sufficient knowledge about transgender persons. It appears that a transgender-friendly environment must be created by providing sufficient knowledge about transgender persons in society and the educational system, and by using the media. It appears that they must be treated equally without discrimination. Likewise, if an environment can be created where transgender persons can live a life of self-respect through their empowerment, the quality of life of transgender persons can be improved, which connects to the prosperity of the country. This study will assist in policy formulation and reform.

australian_english: This article looks to answer the question of whether transgender people in Far-Western Province have been able to come forward in society with their identity, and aims to find out their life experiences and conditions. To do this, in-depth interviews were done with 10 transgender individuals using an unstructured questionnaire through online (Zoom) and phone channels. When it comes to understanding the experiences and conditions of transgender people, different individual situations and experiences turned up. Here are the conclusions of this study: Even though the law has given transgender people the right to equality, no change turned up in practice, behaviour and relationships. Even though the law hasn't recognised same-sex marriage, marriage was found to exist in practice. Even now, most transgender people haven't been able to come out into society with the identity they want, and only a few have been found to have built their identity with society's say-so. Transgender people have had to cop exclusion because of discriminatory behaviour from various areas, and that's been seen to get in the way of their social, educational and economic advancement. Because of this, it hasn't been possible to keep up behaviour and relationships by treating transgender people as part of society, nor has there been a transgender-friendly environment with enough knowledge about transgender people. It looks like a transgender-friendly environment needs to be built by giving enough knowledge about transgender people in society and the education system, and by using the media. It looks like they need to be treated the same as everyone else, no discrimination. Likewise, if an environment can be created where transgender people can live a life of self-respect through their empowerment, the quality of life of transgender people can be improved, which ties into the country's prosperity. This study will help with policy making and reform.
informal_english: This piece sets out to answer a straightforward question: can transgender folks in the Far-West actually come out in society as who they are? And it digs into what their lives are really like. To find out, the researchers had proper deep chats with 10 transgender people, using a loose questionnaire over Zoom and on the phone. What they found was that everyone's experience is different — no two the same. Here's the bottom line: the law says transgender people have a right to equality, but in practice? Nothing's changed. Not in how people behave, not in relationships. Same-sex marriage isn't legal, sure, but people are doing it anyway. Most transgender people still can't show up in society as themselves; only a lucky few have managed to carve out an identity that society accepts. They've been shut out across the board — jobs, school, you name it — because of how people treat them. That's what's holding them back socially, educationally, economically. The upshot? Society still doesn't treat them as full members. There's no real understanding, no transgender-friendly vibe. What's needed? Proper education in schools and communities, media that gets it right, and just treating them like anyone else — no difference. If they're empowered to live with self-respect, their lives get better, and that lifts the whole country. This research should help sort out policy and push for reform.
